NAI-253.meaning: Evaluation-harness tampering: a clock replaced outside the tests, a test report's outcome forced to passed, every collected test marked skipped, a test module skipped unconditionally, the session exit status forced to 0, or an assert method / AssertionError replaced.

NAMING_DRIFT.note: A row names a key, its canonical spelling, a variant spelling, a tier and its sites. T1 (fold alone) certain, T2 (abbreviation map) likely, T3 (one token-edit apart) possible and never counted in the headline. `new` rows (after the launch baseline) are the headline and the seventh zero_signal name; `pre_existing` rows are reported once. Accept from the dash is the only input: `variant` (no row) or `canonical` (the group's canonical flips).

tiers.T3: keys one token-edit apart, every token >= 4 letters; reported, never counted

naming_drift._policy: Naming-drift data type tracker rows (rule id NAMING_DRIFT; PLAN_NAMING_DRIFT_TRACKER_2026-09-29 §D). Its own section, like `path_hacks`: the tracker is permanent and its rows are observations — the disposition vocabulary here is `no_fix_by_design` (the developer renames; CodeRadar never edits the repo it scans), so the row does not sit in `families` (step 18 reads only deciding | context there). The ranker judges false positives (owner 2026-09-30); the abbreviation map (naming_drift/abbreviations.json) is the only knob.

path_hacks._policy: FIX_49 / FIX_50 (owner Q9 / Q10, 2026-09-15). One row per path-hack TYPE, the same shape and the same vocabulary as a rule family: disposition in {deciding, context}; `context` = INFORMATIONAL (published with its warning, never counted as an infraction — D24 / FIX_35 c's shape for relative_import). Per the owner's 2026-09-10 per-(rule, CONTEXT) ruling a row keeps ONE default and may carry `contexts` [{when: {fact: condition}, disposition, warning}] over DISCRETE FACTS the route already measures (role | species | magnitude; ops >= > <= < == != in not_in), first match wins, else the default. A hack type with NO row is deciding — nothing is inferred and the dashboard's literal sets classify it exactly as before. Read by engine_utils.path_hack_disposition; stamped onto every published hack by the circuit daemon; gated by health-check step 18 (disposition_check.py). This section is NEVER a whitelist: a whitelist strips a file from the scan surface, a context row changes only what one hack type means in one measured context.
